neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case revolves around the death of Tanaji Pandurang Rathod, who was assaulted by a mob during a temple event. The deceased was pursued and attacked by a large group of people, resulting in severe injuries and his eventual death. The incident occurred in a village where there was a dispute over agricultural land. The deceased's family members managed to take him to a hospital, where he was found dead. The investigation revealed multiple injuries consistent with the assault, including head trauma and amputations. Bloodstains and weapons were recovered from the scene, and the prosecution attributed specific roles to several accused individuals. The trial court convicted eight accused, while the High Court acquitted others, leading to an appeal.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the sole eye-witness PW-12's testimony was natural, reliable, and corroborated by the recovery of weapons, medical evidence, and other material on record. The case against six accused was completely proved based on her testimony.

quotes.text: The testimony of PW-12 was natural and devoid of any exaggeration and the same is corroborated by the recovery of weapons of offence at the instance of the accused, medical evidence and other material on record

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the testimony of PW-12 was not reliable and that the High Court should have acquitted the accused, as the prosecution failed to establish the common object of the unlawful assembly and the specific roles of the accused.

quotes.text: The High Court has also not rejected her testimony doubting her presence. [Para 17] [380 F-G; 381~A]

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a conviction can be founded on the testimony of a sole witness if it is reliable and corroborated by other evidence, and that the existence of a common object can be determined from the attending facts and circumstances.

quotes.text: The law on the point is well settled that a conviction can well be founded upon the testimony of a sole witness. However, the testimony of a sole witness must be confidence inspiring and beyond suspicion, leaving no doubt in the mind of the Court.
